newsitem.title: USA: Intel first-quarter profit more than doubled.
newsitem.headline: Intel first-quarter profit more than doubled.

text.p: Intel Corp. said Monday its first-quarter profits more than doubled to $1.983 billion from $894 million in the same period last year.
Intel, the world's largest semiconductor maker, said revenues for the three months ended in March rose to $6.4 billion from $4.6 billion a year ago.
Intel's profits were equivalent to $2.20 a share, a 116 percent increase from the $1.02 per share it earned in the year-ago quarter.

The figure was well ahead of Wall Street analysts' concensus forecast of $2.07 a share, according to the First Call service, which tracks analyst predictions. The company's stock gained $3.25 to $133.75 on Nasdaq in anticipation of the strong results. The per share figure also matched the higher so-called "whisper number" -- an unofficial estimate of Wall Street traders.

Intel attributed the record quarterly profit and revenue to higher demands for its most advanced microprocessors, the Pentium processor with MMX media enhancement technology and the Pentium Pro processor.

The Santa Clara, Calif.-based company has had a virtual lock on the market, with more than 80 percent of the world's computers using Intel chips. As such, Intel is widely regarded as a bellwether for the entire technology sector, particularly the personal computer industry.
